## File: src/server/redact.ts

```ts
/** Keys (compared without case, "-" or "_") whose values are always hidden. */
export const SENSITIVE_KEYS = [
  "password", "newpassword", "currentpassword", "oldpassword", "passwordhash",
  "token", "accesstoken", "refreshtoken", "idtoken", "resettoken", "sessiontoken",
  "authorization", "proxyauthorization", "cookie", "setcookie",
  "secret", "clientsecret", "jwtsecret", "apikey", "xapikey", "privatekey",
  "otp", "pin", "cvv", "cardnumber",
] as const;

const SUFFIXES = ["password", "token", "secret", "apikey"];
export const REDACTED = "[redacted]";

const norm = (k: string) => k.toLowerCase().replace(/[-_]/g, "");

export interface RedactOptions {
  /** More keys to hide (any form: "x-api-key", "myField"). */
  keys?: readonly string[];
  /** Maximum depth; deeper values become "[depth]". Default 8. */
  maxDepth?: number;
}

/**
 * A copy of `value` with secrets replaced by "[redacted]", for logs and error reports. Handles nested
 * objects, arrays, Headers-like maps and cycles. Strings that look like bearer tokens are hidden too.
 */
export function redact<T>(value: T, o: RedactOptions = {}): T {
  const extra = new Set((o.keys ?? []).map(norm));
  const exact = new Set<string>([...SENSITIVE_KEYS, ...extra]);
  const maxDepth = o.maxDepth ?? 8;
  const seen = new WeakSet<object>();
  const sensitive = (k: string) => {
    const n = norm(k);
    return exact.has(n) || SUFFIXES.some((s) => n.endsWith(s));
  };

  const walk = (v: unknown, depth: number): unknown => {
    if (typeof v === "string") return /^Bearer\s+\S+/i.test(v) ? "Bearer [redacted]" : v;
    if (v === null || typeof v !== "object") return v;
    if (v instanceof Date) return v;
    if (seen.has(v)) return "[circular]";
    if (depth >= maxDepth) return "[depth]";
    seen.add(v);
    if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.map((x) => walk(x, depth + 1));
    if (v instanceof Map) return Object.fromEntries([...v].map(([k, x]) => [k, sensitive(String(k)) ? REDACTED : walk(x, depth + 1)]));
    if (typeof (v as { forEach?: unknown }).forEach === "function" && typeof (v as { get?: unknown }).get === "function") {
      // Fetch Headers
      const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
      (v as Headers).forEach((x, k) => (out[k] = sensitive(k) ? REDACTED : walk(x, depth + 1)));
      return out;
    }
    if (v instanceof Error) return { name: v.name, message: walk(v.message, depth + 1) };
    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const [k, x] of Object.entries(v)) out[k] = sensitive(k) ? REDACTED : walk(x, depth + 1);
    return out;
  };
  return walk(value, 0) as T;
}

/** "kavita.sharma@example.com" → "k***a@example.com". Returns "" for anything that is not an email. */
export function maskEmail(email: string): string {
  const at = email.lastIndexOf("@");
  if (at < 1) return "";
  const user = email.slice(0, at);
  const shown = user.length <= 2 ? `${user[0]}*` : `${user[0]}***${user[user.length - 1]}`;
  return `${shown}${email.slice(at)}`;
}

/** Keeps the last `visible` digits: "+91 98765 43210" → "******3210". */
export function maskPhone(phone: string, visible = 4): string {
  const digits = phone.replace(/\D/g, "");
  if (!digits) return "";
  const keep = Math.min(visible, Math.max(0, digits.length - 4));
  return "*".repeat(digits.length - keep).slice(-6) + digits.slice(digits.length - keep);
}
```

## File: src/server/signals.ts

```ts
import { createHash, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
import { SIGNALS_HEADER } from "../shared/constants";
import { decodeSignals } from "../shared/signals";
import type { DeviceInfo, DeviceSignals } from "../shared/types";

/** Request headers as Fetch `Headers`, Node's `IncomingHttpHeaders`, or a plain record. */
export type HeaderSource = Headers | { get(name: string): string | null } | Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>;

/** One header value (the first, when repeated); lookup is case-insensitive for records. */
export function headerValue(headers: HeaderSource | undefined, name: string): string | undefined {
  if (!headers) return undefined;
  if (typeof (headers as { get?: unknown }).get === "function") return (headers as { get(n: string): string | null }).get(name) ?? undefined;
  const rec = headers as Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>;
  const lower = name.toLowerCase();
  const key = lower in rec ? lower : Object.keys(rec).find((k) => k.toLowerCase() === lower);
  const v = key === undefined ? undefined : rec[key];
  return Array.isArray(v) ? v[0] : v;
}

/** The request's `DeviceSignals`, or null when the header is missing or invalid. Never throws. */
export function readSignals(headers: HeaderSource | undefined): DeviceSignals | null {
  return decodeSignals(headerValue(headers, SIGNALS_HEADER));
}

/** SHA-256 (base64url) of an id, for storage: the raw device id never sits in the database. */
export function hashSignalId(id: string): string {
  return createHash("sha256").update(id, "utf8").digest("base64url");
}

/**
 * What the server keeps on a session (and its refresh token) to recognise the device later.
 * Store it as it is; it holds no raw id.
 */
export interface SignalBinding {
  deviceIdHash: string;
  fingerprint: string;
  device: DeviceInfo;
  /** Tab id at login, hashed; informational (a refresh may come from another tab of the same browser). */
  tabIdHash: string;
}

export function bindSignals(signals: DeviceSignals): SignalBinding {
  return {
    deviceIdHash: hashSignalId(signals.deviceId),
    fingerprint: signals.fingerprint,
    device: { ...signals.device },
    tabIdHash: hashSignalId(signals.tabId),
  };
}

/**
 * - `same`: same device id and fingerprint.
 * - `changed`: same device id, but the fingerprint, OS, browser or form factor changed (log it; a browser
 *   update, new screen or language change does this).
 * - `other-device`: a different device id (reject: the token was copied to another browser).
 * - `missing`: the request has no valid signals but the session has a binding.
 * - `unbound`: the session has no binding (created before signals existed, or by a non-browser client).
 */
export type SignalVerdict = "same" | "changed" | "other-device" | "missing" | "unbound";

export interface SignalCheck {
  verdict: SignalVerdict;
  /** What differs: "deviceId", "fingerprint", "os", "browser", "mobile", "timezone", "language", "screen". */
  changes: string[];
  /** True for "same" and "changed"; false otherwise. A caller decides what to do with "missing"/"unbound". */
  sameDevice: boolean;
}

const eq = (a: string, b: string) => {
  const x = Buffer.from(a), y = Buffer.from(b);
  return x.length === y.length && timingSafeEqual(x, y);
};

/** Compares a stored binding with a request's signals. Pure; never throws. */
export function checkSignals(binding: SignalBinding | null | undefined, incoming: DeviceSignals | null | undefined): SignalCheck {
  if (!binding) return { verdict: "unbound", changes: [], sameDevice: false };
  if (!incoming) return { verdict: "missing", changes: [], sameDevice: false };
  if (!eq(binding.deviceIdHash, hashSignalId(incoming.deviceId))) return { verdict: "other-device", changes: ["deviceId"], sameDevice: false };
  const changes: string[] = [];
  if (binding.fingerprint !== incoming.fingerprint) changes.push("fingerprint");
  for (const k of ["os", "browser", "mobile", "timezone", "language", "screen"] as const) {
    if (binding.device?.[k] !== incoming.device[k]) changes.push(k);
  }
  return { verdict: changes.length ? "changed" : "same", changes, sameDevice: true };
}

export interface SignalPolicy {
  /** Reject a session used with another device id. Default true. */
  rejectOtherDevice?: boolean;
  /** Reject when signals are missing but the session is bound. Default false (old clients keep working). */
  requireSignals?: boolean;
}

/**
 * Applies a policy to a check: `allow` false means end the session; `log` true means write an audit
 * entry (every verdict except "same" and "unbound").
 */
export function decide(check: SignalCheck, policy: SignalPolicy = {}): { allow: boolean; log: boolean } {
  const rejectOther = policy.rejectOtherDevice ?? true;
  switch (check.verdict) {
    case "same":
    case "unbound":
      return { allow: true, log: false };
    case "changed":
      return { allow: true, log: true };
    case "other-device":
      return { allow: !rejectOther, log: true };
    case "missing":
      return { allow: !policy.requireSignals, log: true };
  }
}
```

## File: src/server/tls.ts

```ts
// TLS client fingerprint (JA4 / JA3). It comes from the TLS ClientHello, so no browser code can collect
// it: the server that terminates TLS computes it. Behind a reverse proxy, that proxy (nginx with a JA4
// module, Envoy, CloudFront, Cloudflare) passes it on in a request header, which is read here with the
// same trust model as X-Forwarded-For: only when the request came through a trusted proxy.
import { headerValue, type HeaderSource } from "./signals";

export type TlsFingerprintKind = "ja4" | "ja3" | "other";

export interface TlsFingerprint {
  /** "ja4" (e.g. t13d1516h2_8daaf6152771_e5627efa2ab1), "ja3" (32-hex MD5), or another proxy-specific form. */
  kind: TlsFingerprintKind;
  /** The fingerprint as the proxy sent it (JA4 / JA3 lower-cased). Not secret, but store a hash (see auth-kit). */
  value: string;
}

export interface TlsFingerprintOptions {
  headers?: HeaderSource;
  /**
   * The header the TLS-terminating proxy sets, e.g. "x-ja4". Unset (the default): no fingerprint.
   * The proxy must SET it (overwrite), never pass a client's value through.
   */
  header?: string | null;
  /** Reverse proxies in front of the server (as for clientIp). 0 (default): the header is ignored, because any client can send it. */
  trustedHops?: number;
}

const JA4 = /^[tqd][0-9a-z]{2}[di]\d{4}[0-9a-z]{2}_[0-9a-f]{12}_[0-9a-f]{12}$/;
const JA3 = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/;
const OTHER = /^[A-Za-z0-9_.:,+\/=-]{8,256}$/;

/** Classifies and normalises one header value; null when it is malformed or oversized. Never throws. */
export function parseTlsFingerprint(raw: string | null | undefined): TlsFingerprint | null {
  if (typeof raw !== "string" || raw.length > 256) return null;
  const v = raw.trim();
  const lower = v.toLowerCase();
  if (JA4.test(lower)) return { kind: "ja4", value: lower };
  if (JA3.test(lower)) return { kind: "ja3", value: lower };
  return OTHER.test(v) ? { kind: "other", value: v } : null;
}

/**
 * The request's TLS fingerprint from the proxy header, or null: no header configured, no trusted proxy
 * (`trustedHops` 0), header missing (TLS terminated somewhere that does not compute it), or malformed.
 * Never throws; a missing fingerprint is never an error.
 */
export function readTlsFingerprint(o: TlsFingerprintOptions): TlsFingerprint | null {
  if (!o.header || Math.floor(o.trustedHops ?? 0) < 1) return null;
  return parseTlsFingerprint(headerValue(o.headers, o.header));
}
```

## File: src/shared/constants.ts

```ts
/** HTTP header that carries the encoded `DeviceSignals` (see `encodeSignals`). */
export const SIGNALS_HEADER = "x-mgpl-signals";

/** Limits enforced by `decodeSignals`; anything larger or malformed is rejected. */
export const SIGNAL_LIMITS = {
  /** Encoded header value, in characters. */
  header: 2048,
  /** Any single string inside DeviceInfo, and `app`. */
  field: 64,
} as const;

/** Ids are 16 to 64 base64url characters (a UUID with or without dashes also fits). */
export const ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$/;
/** Fingerprints are 32 lowercase hex characters. */
export const FINGERPRINT_PATTERN = /^[0-9a-f]{32}$/;
```

## File: src/shared/crypto.ts

```ts
// Primitives that run unchanged in browsers, Node.js >= 20, workers and React Native with Web Crypto:
// only globalThis.crypto, TextEncoder, btoa and atob. No Buffer, no node: imports.

const enc = new TextEncoder();
const dec = new TextDecoder();

function webCrypto(): Crypto {
  const c = (globalThis as { crypto?: Crypto }).crypto;
  if (!c?.getRandomValues) throw new Error("security-kit: Web Crypto (globalThis.crypto) is not available");
  return c;
}

/** base64url (RFC 4648 §5, no padding) of bytes or of a UTF-8 string. */
export function toBase64Url(input: Uint8Array | string): string {
  const bytes = typeof input === "string" ? enc.encode(input) : input;
  let bin = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) bin += String.fromCharCode(bytes[i]!);
  return btoa(bin).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
}

/** Bytes of a base64url string; null when it is not valid base64url. */
export function fromBase64Url(value: string): Uint8Array | null {
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/.test(value) || value.length % 4 === 1) return null;
  const b64 = value.replace(/-/g, "+").replace(/_/g, "/") + "===".slice((value.length + 3) % 4);
  try {
    const bin = atob(b64);
    const out = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) out[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
    return out;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

export const utf8 = {
  encode: (s: string) => enc.encode(s),
  decode: (b: Uint8Array) => dec.decode(b),
};

/** Cryptographically random bytes. */
export function randomBytes(n: number): Uint8Array {
  const out = new Uint8Array(n);
  webCrypto().getRandomValues(out);
  return out;
}

/** A random id: `bytes` random bytes as base64url (16 bytes → 22 characters, 128 bits). */
export function randomId(bytes = 16): string {
  return toBase64Url(randomBytes(bytes));
}

/** SHA-256 as lowercase hex (async, Web Crypto). */
export async function sha256Hex(input: string | Uint8Array): Promise<string> {
  const data = typeof input === "string" ? enc.encode(input) : input;
  const digest = new Uint8Array(await webCrypto().subtle.digest("SHA-256", data as BufferSource));
  let hex = "";
  for (const b of digest) hex += b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0");
  return hex;
}

/**
 * Compares two strings in time that depends only on their lengths. Use it for hashes and ids
 * of a fixed length; a different length returns false at once.
 */
export function constantTimeEqual(a: string, b: string): boolean {
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  let diff = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) diff |= a.charCodeAt(i) ^ b.charCodeAt(i);
  return diff === 0;
}

/** JSON with object keys sorted at every level, so equal values always serialise identically. */
export function canonicalJson(value: unknown): string {
  if (value === null || typeof value !== "object") return JSON.stringify(value) ?? "null";
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(canonicalJson).join(",")}]`;
  const obj = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const keys = Object.keys(obj).filter((k) => obj[k] !== undefined).sort();
  return `{${keys.map((k) => `${JSON.stringify(k)}:${canonicalJson(obj[k])}`).join(",")}}`;
}
```

## File: src/shared/signals.ts

```ts
import { FINGERPRINT_PATTERN, ID_PATTERN, SIGNAL_LIMITS, SIGNALS_HEADER } from "./constants";
import { fromBase64Url, toBase64Url, utf8 } from "./crypto";
import type { DeviceInfo, DeviceSignals } from "./types";

/** Header value for `DeviceSignals`: base64url of their JSON. */
export function encodeSignals(signals: DeviceSignals): string {
  return toBase64Url(JSON.stringify(signals));
}

/** `{ "x-mgpl-signals": encodeSignals(signals) }`, ready to merge into request headers. */
export function signalHeaders(signals: DeviceSignals): Record<string, string> {
  return { [SIGNALS_HEADER]: encodeSignals(signals) };
}

// printable ASCII and common Unicode letters; no control characters, no angle brackets
const SAFE_TEXT = /^[^\u0000-\u001f\u007f<>]*$/;
const text = (v: unknown): string | null => (typeof v === "string" && v.length <= SIGNAL_LIMITS.field && SAFE_TEXT.test(v) ? v : null);

/** Checks an untrusted value and returns clean `DeviceInfo`, or null if any field is wrong. */
export function parseDeviceInfo(v: unknown): DeviceInfo | null {
  if (!v || typeof v !== "object") return null;
  const d = v as Record<string, unknown>;
  const os = text(d.os), browser = text(d.browser), browserVersion = text(d.browserVersion);
  const language = text(d.language), timezone = text(d.timezone), screen = text(d.screen);
  if (os === null || browser === null || browserVersion === null || language === null || timezone === null || screen === null) return null;
  if (typeof d.mobile !== "boolean") return null;
  return { os, browser, browserVersion, mobile: d.mobile, language, timezone, screen };
}

/** Checks an untrusted object and returns clean `DeviceSignals` (unknown keys dropped), or null. */
export function parseSignals(v: unknown): DeviceSignals | null {
  if (!v || typeof v !== "object" || Array.isArray(v)) return null;
  const s = v as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (s.v !== 1) return null;
  if (typeof s.deviceId !== "string" || !ID_PATTERN.test(s.deviceId)) return null;
  if (typeof s.tabId !== "string" || !ID_PATTERN.test(s.tabId)) return null;
  if (typeof s.fingerprint !== "string" || !FINGERPRINT_PATTERN.test(s.fingerprint)) return null;
  const device = parseDeviceInfo(s.device);
  if (!device) return null;
  let app: string | undefined;
  if (s.app !== undefined) {
    const a = text(s.app);
    if (a === null) return null;
    app = a;
  }
  return { v: 1, deviceId: s.deviceId, tabId: s.tabId, fingerprint: s.fingerprint, device, ...(app !== undefined ? { app } : {}) };
}

/** Decodes and validates a header value; null when missing, too long or malformed. Never throws. */
export function decodeSignals(value: string | null | undefined): DeviceSignals | null {
  if (typeof value !== "string" || !value || value.length > SIGNAL_LIMITS.header) return null;
  const bytes = fromBase64Url(value.trim());
  if (!bytes) return null;
  try {
    return parseSignals(JSON.parse(utf8.decode(bytes)));
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}
```

## File: src/shared/types.ts

```ts
/** Coarse facts about the device and browser. No canvas, audio, WebGL or font probing. */
export interface DeviceInfo {
  /** "Windows" | "macOS" | "iOS" | "Android" | "ChromeOS" | "Linux" | "Other" */
  os: string;
  /** "Chrome" | "Edge" | "Firefox" | "Safari" | "Opera" | "Samsung Internet" | "Other" */
  browser: string;
  /** Major version only, e.g. "131"; "" when unknown. */
  browserVersion: string;
  mobile: boolean;
  /** BCP 47 language tag, e.g. "en-IN". */
  language: string;
  /** IANA time zone, e.g. "Asia/Kolkata". */
  timezone: string;
  /** "1920x1080" (larger side first, so rotating a phone does not change it); "" when unknown. */
  screen: string;
}

/**
 * The security signals a client sends with login and refresh (and may send with every request).
 * Collected by `@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit/browser`, read by `@mgpl-diagnostics/security-kit/server`.
 */
export interface DeviceSignals {
  /** Signal format version. */
  v: 1;
  /** Random id kept in the browser's persistent storage: one per browser profile. */
  deviceId: string;
  /** Random id kept in session storage: one per tab. */
  tabId: string;
  /** SHA-256 (hex, 32 chars) of the coarse device attributes; changes when the device's setup changes. */
  fingerprint: string;
  device: DeviceInfo;
  /** The app's own version, when it sets one. */
  app?: string;
}
```
